mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment rate > 4.5% historically precedes equity downturns
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in industrial production (INDPRO > 100) and residential housing starts (HOUST > 1300) signal robust economic activity that boosts corporate profits and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Industrial production and housing starts correlate with equity market strength
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 100 and HOUST > 1300 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate above 4.0% during monetary tightening cycles signals increased cost of capital that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payrolls (PAYEMS > 159000) indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Payroll growth correlates with equity market performance
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 159000 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 320 signals persistent inflation that triggers central bank rate hikes, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 320 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A high residential sales volume (RSAFS > 700000) combined with low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 4.0%) indicates strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy that jointly boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Residential sales and low rates correlate with equity gains
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 700000 and FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 during supply contraction regimes signals reduced manufacturing output and lower corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Industrial Production and Equity Market Correlation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
